quizGuardRationale: Pairs on new articles are direct, symmetric and nontransitive. Baseline declarations are untouched. Guards concern overlapping English labels or actual Japanese meanings, not unrestricted substitution.

代わる protects taking another's place, substitute, replace and exchange labels across grammatical viewpoints; 変わる is a distinct change identity rather than automatically an interchangeable replacement spelling.
間隔 protects actual interval/space/gap labels on 間, 空き and 差; homophonous 感覚 is not excluded merely for its sound.
感激 protects actual moving/impression/admiration and emotion/feeling labels. A deep emotional response is not every feeling, but an unmarked emotion answer is not uniquely wrong.
鑑賞 protects English appreciation ambiguity with gratitude and the broader see/look label. 観賞's complete family supports a comparison, not a nonexistent card reference.
感ずる protects feeling/sensing/thinking, moving/impressed and subjective feeling labels. A noun/verb difference alone does not sense-restrict the bare quiz prompt.
感想 protects actual impression, opinion, thought/view and subjective feeling labels; opinions and responses to experiences overlap without forming one Japanese substitution set.
観測 protects actual observation, investigation/measurement and assessment/prediction/opinion labels. Scientific observation and forecasting are distinct uses retained in teaching.
官庁 protects actual government agency/authority and generic office labels; complete 事務所 and オフィス families support office, not an invented private-only restriction.
勘違い protects mistake/misunderstanding/error labels including 失敗's actual mistake/blunder meaning, not merely the shared topic of undesirable outcomes.
缶詰/缶 protects both can/container ambiguity and 缶's explicit canned-food abbreviation sense.
観念 protects idea/thought, actual awareness/sense, resignation/giving-up/readiness and acceptance labels. Accepting an unavoidable outcome need not imply agreement or approval.
乾杯 protects the unqualified English toast label on あぶる and 煎る, not Japanese synonymy with cooking. 飲む and 干す are not automatically excluded merely because toasting can include drinking.
看板 protects sign/notice, reputation/name/public-face, feature and actual outward-appearance/show labels. It does not collapse every physical board or business word into a synonym.

寒帯 versus 熱帯/温帯 and 関西 versus 関東 are meaningful climatic/geographic contrasts, not exclusions merely for belonging to a common category. Other comparison candidates remain evidence without being declared guards.
sourceAccessLimits: Receipts are author access, not independent reviewer access. Search summaries, failed lookups and heading-only sections do not establish definitions.
Nineteen new articles and level-only reuse of 乾燥 for explicit drying/dryness senses 1-2; reuse is not whole-article recertification.

Twelve primary-form N2 pairs for new articles; 乾/乾燥 is additionally linked for the reused article, while 燥/乾燥 was already linked. Useful 替わる/換わる alias backlinks target explicitly taught forms and are not additional primary-form pairs.
Missing component cards 隔, 激, 鑑, 勘 and 看 remain in written-kanji metadata. No speculative kanji/stroke additions or invented constituent readings.
勘違い and 缶詰 use the format's on-first kango category while explicitly explaining mixed formation. 缶's recorded loan origins are not silently converted into Chinese etymology.
Existing 感覚, 缶, 意見, 感じる and the kaeru comparison gain narrow navigation only. Existing IDs, primary readings, titles, easier levels and original exclusion lists are preserved.
Complete families retain unselected spellings/readings and specialist/historical flags. Dictionary order/priority does not establish measured frequency.

Original examples are teaching sentences, not corpus quotations. Lexical evidence and structural validation are not native-speaker certification, an executed app draw or an official modern JLPT syllabus.
